ChopDawg

Timeline

JIRA

Tools
My Role

Lead Product Design

Strategy

UX/UI Design

ChopDawg is a design agency that has partnered with startups and enterprises around the world to launch 400+ next-generation apps. As a Product Designer at ChopDawg, I've played a key role in designing impactful solutions for 10+ digital products across mobile apps, web apps, admin apps, SAAS, and websites. Leading user research and creating detailed product plans, I empower clients to enhance their businesses. 

Overview
Outcome

Working at ChopDawg across 10+ projects has been an exciting endeavor that has helped my diversify my skills from end to end product development. Specifically, I was able to hone into my design process & helped the team reduce development time by 15% and successfully streamlined my project timelines by 20%. Over the year, I've also leveraged AI tools to empower my design process & took on mentoring junior designers on stakeholder management & design efficiencies. 

02

MINDFUL DRIVING NAVIGATION APP

In Development

Aligning user needs with client vision

My role spanned from concept to reality, developing a mobile app with CarPlay and Android Auto compatibility. I was involved from inception, participating in client consultations, scoping, and proposal writing for a unique navigation app encouraging mindful driving.

 

Key challenges included translating the clients' abstract vision into tangible design and balancing innovative features with road safety. Despite these hurdles, we crafted a seamless navigation experience with personalized audio prompts and situation-specific cues.

​

As a outcome, the project successfully merged spiritual mindfulness with practical navigation, creating a distinctive product in the market. The app's effectiveness was validated through moderated usability tests, achieving a 92% success rate.

**Project details including name/branding have been modified due to NDA**

Reflecting on project outcomes

Over the span of my time at ChopDawg, I've put on multiple hats while working in a fast paced setting. It would be difficult to put into words the various ways I've grown as a designer & a professional but here are some of the key learnings.

04

DESIGNER LEARNINGS

01

UX Research without access to users

In startup projects, limited time and budget often constrained user research. This taught me to adapt, using desk research & available feedback to minimize assumptions. Stakeholder testing also proved valuable, offering insights while building empathy for the target audience—a win-win approach.

02

Annotate. Annotate. Annotate.

To resolve friction and misinterpretations during developer hand-offs, I introduced detailed screen annotations and dev notes. This simple addition streamlined alignment and significantly reduced back-and-forth communication.

03

Anticipating needs & being proactive

Working on multiple projects, PMs & stakeholders, being able to anticipate next steps was a game changer. By being self-aware & stepping up to facilitate collaboration and proposing solutions before being asked, I learned to UX the process itself, enhance team efficiency and project outcomes. 

03

ED-TECH VIRTUAL LEARNING WEB APP

In Testing & QA

Reimagining virtual circle-time for kids

My role as Lead Product Designer for Storyo encompassed product design and strategy, transforming a vision for family-friendly content into a responsive web app. I led all aspects of design from wireframes to high-fidelity mockups, creating a scalable platform with a credit-based subscription model.

 

Key challenges included designing an intuitive credit system and crafting a responsive interface that appealed to both parents and children. We balanced flexibility with simplicity while ensuring engaging content discovery for all ages.

 

As a outcome, the final product successfully merged entertainment with accessibility We also identified ways to help students leverage government education aid to further their learning on Storyo. Storyo will soon be launching as a unique offering in the family entertainment market, providing a customizable platform for diverse content consumption.

01

A MARKETPLACE FOR HOBBYISTS & COLLECTORS

In Development

Re-establishing client trust

My role as a UX/UI Designer for this project was to realign the deliverables with the project timeline while identifying gaps in the user journey. I joined this project mid-development, focusing on creating a seamless marketplace experience for hobbyists and collectors.

​

Key challenges included acclimating to a new organization, maintaining client satisfaction despite frequent team changes, and preventing delays amidst multiple client-driven design pivots. Despite these hurdles, I identified and refined user flow gaps, creating a smoother experience.

​

As an outcome, I delivered high-quality design assets that better reflected the brand, which helped re-establish client trust. Additionally, I took on the mentorship of a junior designer, improving their design efficiency and stakeholder management skills. This project not only enhanced the product but also strengthened our team's capabilities and client relationships.

**Project details including name/branding have been modified due to NDA**

Empowering parents to travel confidently & efficiently

Starling Assist

24 Weeks

Timeline

Figma

Miro

Qualtrics

Tools
My Role

Product Strategy

UX Design

UI & Branding

Starling Assist is an in-airport concierge assistance that aims to help parents take a break, navigate easier at the airport and bring focus back to the family. It is powered by a mobile app and a sleek, NFC based safety band to assure parents throughout their journey. As a solo designer on this masters thesis project, I spearheaded both the strategic direction and product design.

Overview
Outcome

Humanized airport experience for 62% of millennial parents travelling with kids 5 years or younger.
Significantly decreased parents anxiety about handling kids at the airport.
92% parents felt more confident and assured in their travel due to Starling Assist.
Instead of expected 1%, 4% of website visitors signed up for early access to service.

OVERVIEW
Goodbye to airport hassles and hello to stress-free family travel! 🌟✈️
CHALLENGE

"Traveling solo with kids is really intimidating & anxiety provoking for me, I'm never doing that again!" - A Parent 

​

One of the largest group of audience airports cater to are family travelers. Despite this, parents are also the largest group to have a traumatic & dreaded experience at the airports. I was curious to explore this discrepancy and figure out the hows, whats & whys. With more families planning to travel frequently, it presents a huge opportunity of growth for airports as well. The challenge was to identify why parents tend to have such an anxious experience and how I can offer a solution that is viable for airports and desirable for parents. 

WHAT I DID

I spearheaded this challenge as a part of my masters thesis project over a timeline of 24 weeks consisting of thorough user research, product discovery and product development.

​

Navigating the ambiguity, I employed rigorous design processes to deeply understand user experiences and pinpoint key opportunities. Through extensive research, ideation and iterative prototyping, I crafted Starling Assist - a scalable, human-centered solution revolutionizing the airport ordeal for families, especially solo parents with children. This innovative design garnered high praise for empathetically enhancing one of life's most stressful journeys within the complex airport environment.

View final design

DESIGN PROCESS

01

Desk Research / User Surveys / Interviews / Current State Analysis / Empathy Maps

Problem Discovery

Forming the foundation of defining the right problem, I focused on learning as much as I can about the different facets of the problem by discovering the Whats, Whys & Whos. I was also looking to inform my big picture view on the space as well as looking for any co-dependent areas that could impact the problem.

02

Equipped with the answers of my Whats & Whys and an arsenal of knowledge about the problem space from several aspects, I began untangling the complexities down to the root cause of the issue. This became my lighthouse in keeping the solution process focused and clear.

Problem Definition

Problem Statement / Ideation methods

03

Guided by the clear vision of the problem at hand, I began reimagining the experience to be empathetic & delightful for users. My goal was to ideate a solution that is feasible, viable and impactful enough to move the needle. I was focused on answering the “What ifs” and setting realistic objectives & vision for the product to be successful.

Solution Discovery & Scoping

Storyboarding / Scoping & Strategy / Information Arch / Success Metrics (KPIs & KEIs)

04

Execution & Testing

Wireframes / Visual & Brand Strategy / Prototyping / User Simulation / Usability Testing

At this stage, it was time to bring the product to life. Based on all the insights and data gathered I began designing the mobile app for Starling Assist as well as non-gui aspects of the product. This stage was also the moment of truth as I began testing the product in the market and gathering feedback from parents, caregivers & stakeholders.

The who, what, & why

I started off with desk research and exploring the inner dynamic of the airports and what are the existing services provided to travelers. I explored several social media forums, articles and blogs to gain a perspective on parents journey and current state - what is working vs. what is not. This formed the foundation of forming a big picture and understanding the various factors I was working with.

PROBLEM DISCOVERY

01

"We were standing in line in security, on the verge of tears because Wyatt was screaming & James was exhausted!"

It's a one-man army situation

"I was so upset and shocked! So rude, insensitive and inhuman!! "

Lack of empathy from staff

"It was disastrous and involved several meltdowns from both children & me. The long hours on first flight were enough to completely drain the life out of me but the stop at Philadelphia airport really did me in"

Emotionally & physically draining

"I had to walk for what felt like several miles, with a crying infant in my arms, to get her pushchair from baggage reclaim...I sobbed for the whole two hours car ride home."

Existing services are ineffective

PARENT CURRENT STATE AT THE AIRPORT

To further understand why the experience is so intimidating I looked at several different parent travel forums, articles & blogs that shared some of the experiences parents continue to have. Here are the key findings

USER RESEARCH - FINDINGS & INSIGHTS

To get a better understanding on parents behaviors on airport & the challenges faced, I conducted 2 semi- structured interviews with parents who had recently traveled solo with their children & compared that to parents travelling together. Additionally,  50+ individuals completed the survey. Here are the key takeaways.

- one of the parents during interview

"Why does it have to be so hard, Why are there no service available when it comes to the tiniest humans & their caregivers"

Top 3 stressors

for parents at the airport were handling luggage, cranky kids & security checks

Prioritizing children's happiness above all can strain parents' mental and physical health, potentially impacting tasks such as navigating immigration checks.

69%

of parents felt stressed more than usual when travelling alone with children

A major reason for this is due to the overwhelming amount of tasks a parents takes on single handedly amidst the 15+ hours of travel. Simple tasks like going to the washroom becomes a mammoth task requiring mental planning & preparation

This is primarily because there are often just 1 - 2 play areas on the entire airport. Which means if its not close to the boarding gates, its never used. 

of parents do not find airport play areas to be helpful

60%

VISZUALIZING THE PAIN POINTS

I knew the numbers alone feel dry & ineffective in building empathy or conveying the challenges parents face. So, to make the concepts more relatable to stakeholders, I combined key takeaways from user research  and developed a persona for "Struggling Sara" and an empathy map reflecting her journey. This storytelling approach helped bring the data points to life in a meaningful way.

Empathy map takeaways

Persona - Struggling Sara

Honing down on the problem

Honing down on the pain points, I established my problem statement as the guiding statement towards the solution. On the business front, I expanded my perspective to the big picture and why airports should even look out for family travelers.

02

PROBLEM DEFINITION

PROBLEM STATEMENT

Layovers leave solo travelling parents frazzled - torn between seizing precious downtime and remaining hyper-vigilant over kids and baggage. How can we provide parents with peaceful respite during layovers?

WHY SHOULD AIRPORTS CARE? - THE BIG PICTURE

On the flip side of the coin, it was important to understand how unhappy family travelers affect airports & its business goals.

 

I found that public airports are held accountable by ratings & a good reputation can help them achieve a global benchmark of Airport Excellence such as Skytrax. An example of this is the Changi Airport in Singapore. The quality of airport, ratings & reputation directly impact the traveler flow as well as the revenue an airport can generate

CHALLENGE

50% of airport revenue comes from retail & airport service. With family travel making up for 376 million trips globally, unhappy families could significantly impact an airport's reputation and its revenue generation.

OPPORTUNITY

Airport success relies on revenue, ratings, and catering to family travelers. To enhance passenger trust, loyalty, and overall airport reputation, it's crucial for airports to better assist solo parents during layovers, ultimately boosting revenue.

Research reflected that parents often doubt generic services can meet their children's needs. We solve this by pairing families with assistants who have relevant experience and interests, ensuring a better connection with kids.

PERSONALIZED SESSIONS

Connecting parents with assistants suitable to their needs.

Assistants receive ‘Parent notes’ with special considerations & preferences for the session.

Assistants maintain a 4 star rating - assuring a high quality service

Building trust with detailed assistant profiles

Experience summary: Each assistant's profile shows their skills and past work.

Parent reviews: Feedback from other families builds trust and keeps assistants accountable.

In-app chat: Parents/assistants can talk directly to build rapport & get acquainted before sessions.

EARLY INTERACTION

The safety band serves to verify parent - assistant identities at the airport through unique RFID sensors that are linked to their profiles. The bands also enable iBeacon based location tracking inside airports for increased transparency & safety.

SAFETY BANDS FOR ADVANCED SECURITY

safe zone keeps everyone within a safe/accessible distance

In-session screen

Pre-trip screen with upcoming session

Initial onboarding screen with no bookings

The home screen dynamically changes depending on where the user is in their journey. This helps simplify the app and avoid overwhelming user with multiple flows & navigation challenges.

DYNAMIC DASHBOARD
Final Design & Decisions
Reflecting on project outcomes

Airports have always been an intriguing design study so the project was a fun challenge while helping me grow as a designer & strategist. I gained insight on the nuances that must be dealt with when designing in a restricted landscape such as airports.  Here's some of my key learnings.

05

DESIGNER LEARNINGS

01

Staying rooted in reality

As a designer we can often feel like our solutions should be a catch all ideal take but that is not always feasible. Through this project I learned that sometimes what matters is where we can move the needle even at the slightest - that is enough for start!

02

Learning backend & dev planning

In order to maintain product's feasibility, I had to quickly educate myself on different backend functionalities & tools such as APIs, SDKs, & database modeling. While this was challenging, it was fun and made it easier to scope strategically & plan for development.

03

Navigating ambiguity 

Working in such a broad problem space with so many uncertainties has honed in my ability to navigate ambiguity through strategy of prioritization and being adaptable to situations as they evolve. 

04

Designing beyond screens

Due to the service nature of the app, I had to keep the big picture of the users experience in mind at all steps. The overlap of digital, spatial and service design were great learnings on complex design solutions.

Scoping & Strategizing

My goal was to ask "Is this the right It?" at every step of brainstorming and strategy, while exploring the varied range of solutions and its effectiveness in moving the needle. I believe this is the most important step that requires careful consideration & plays a key factor in determining allocation of resources and feasibility of the solution.

03

SOLUTION DISCOVERY & SCOPING

Designing for trust was the biggest challenge 

As I began ideating and reflecting back on the key issues of users from research, I soon realized any solution will require a mechanism for gaining trust - a parent's trust! Getting some creative brains together, I decided to do multiple brainstorming session.

 

Unfortunately however, none of the brainstorming ideas were the way to go. They did however spark creativity and inspiration that led me to the final solution.

Visualizing the conception of solution

Being a visual person, I find that storyboarding the solution is one of the most helpful methods to play out how the solution functions. I also find it helpful for figuring out the needs & considerations to keep in mind while designing

​

Take a look at the journey of Struggling Sara, a mom, planning to travel solo with her child. Her airport journey becomes relaxed with the help of an expert assistant that allows her to take a break without having to worry about her child.

Scoping the key features & service flow

Upon validating the solution concept with the peers through storyboard, I began scoping out the details further. Specifically, I utilized the MoSCoW Method for features. I also began determining the key experience indicators using the HEART Model. This proved to be critical in understanding product's impact.

Moscow method

Information Architecture for the app

Service Blueprint

Mid-fi wireframes

Early testing = reduced risk, higher success rate

As I approached towards final product design, I decided to put it to test early and get real feedback from parents & childcare assistants by performing a service simulation and mechanical turk. The results provided valuable feedback that enhanced and improved the MVP of Startling Assist. Upon feedback from the testing brought the product to life with UI & branding, turning wireframes into hi-fidelity prototypes.

04

EXECUTION & TESTING

CHALLENGE

How do you test for an in-airport service without being in an airport?

An accurate testing environment is key to producing accurate & reliable results but due to security reasons, it was impossible for me to run this simulation at the airport. 

SOLTUTION

The crowds of the mall sparked an idea! Mimicking the airport environment at a super mall setting was the closest way to observe and get feedback on effectiveness of Starling Assist for parents. This resulted in valuable insights that would further enhance the service.

SERVICE SIMULATION

In order to test early and get practical insights from the in-airport interaction between parents and assistant, I ran a simulation with 3 parents with children and experienced childcare assistant at a local mall. The parents were asked to drop their children with assistants with the ability to check in through text and even extend the service up to 10 mins if needed.

​

Hypothesis: The service will receive a minimum of 3.5 NPS rating from participants. Additionally, the participant will wear the safety bands for the entire session.

RESULTS

5/5 Net Promotor Score

from happy parents & assistants

Despite the short time frame of the service, parents felt assured & confident when taking a break away from their child. Parents also mentioned increased efficiency in task completions due to reduced childcare stress.

2/3 parents opted-in 

to extend their Starling sessions

Parent exit interviews showed constant communication during sessions was crucial for reassurance. "I could work guilt-free, knowing my son was cared for and happy."

TAKEAWAYS

01

Allows parents greater flexibility

to move around and attend to various needs - such as freshening up, getting food, or handling other tasks - with less restriction

02

Parent Notes

or parent preferences prior to session start were crucial in having clear expectations & keeping the assistants informed

03

Movement flexibility for assistants

proved to be important to better engage kids - this can be challenging with luggage

04

Future opportunities

of leveraging partnerships with airports for stroller, carts and toys can further improve the user experience 

"It was comforting & allowed me to relax. Having touchpoints with the assistant through texts & photos was assuring."
- Isha (parent)

Revitalizing school-community partnerships

Big Picture Philadelphia

24 Weeks

Timeline

Figma

Miro

SemRush

Tools
My Role

UX Design Lead

UX Research

Leading a team of three designers, I redesigned the BPP's website, overhauling the information architecture, resolving usability issues, and crafting a content strategy for improved clarity. My particular emphasis was on stakeholder management & aligning our strategy and designs with the broader vision, ensuring a harmonious balance between the organization's objectives and the needs of its users.

Overview
Outcome

The overall revamped website design and IA resulted in a significant, 89% increase in usability and website engagement and a 30% increase in direct success rate for key task completion. We also proposed an AR based service extension for the schools to increase student learning outcomes.

OVERVIEW
Reimagining mentor & donor engagement flow at Philadelphia schools
CHALLENGE

Big Picture Philadelphia (BPP) is a nonprofit educational organization dedicated to achieving educational equity and accessibility for more than 400 students in the Philadelphia area. Central to their approach is offering students real-world, project-based opportunities coupled with professional mentorship and hands-on experience.

​

While the school offers a unique learning model through community engagement, the key touchpoints such as website & intake forms proved to be major friction points. This was a serious problem as it directly impacted student learning outcomes & missed opportunities of growth for students & organization.

WHAT I DID

Leading a team of three designers, I set out to redesign the BPP's website, overhauling the information architecture, resolving usability issues, and crafting a content strategy for improved clarity. My particular emphasis was on stakeholder management & aligning our strategy and designs with the broader vision, ensuring a harmonious balance between the organization's objectives and the needs of its users.

​

The overall revamped website design and IA resulted in a significant, 89% increase in usability and website engagement. We also proposed an AR based service extension for the schools to increase student learning outcomes. 

View final design

DESIGN PROCESS

01

Current State Usability Test / Current State Analysis / Stakeholder Interview / User Journey / User Persona

Problem Discovery

New to the non-profit organization, I started off with learning the school's background and how it functions. This helped me ask the write questions for stakeholder interview and get insight on the purpose of the website & its target users. Doing a content audit also highlighted what was working & not working on the existing website.

02

After gathering insights from research synthesis and journey maps, the pain points & issues such as confusing content & areas of usability failures were clear to me. The next step was to hone in on the content strategy statement and collaborate with team on establishing clear design goals to guide us.

Problem Definition

Content Strategy / Ideation methods / Competitive Analysis

03

Guided by data & research insights, I initiated salvaging the website and proposing the new information architecture & content strategy. These elements combined guided the final design and set realistic benchmarks to assess project success.

Solution Discovery & Scoping

Scoping & Strategy / Information Arch / Card Sorting / AB Testing

04

Execution & Testing

Wireframes / Visual & Brand Strategy /  Usability Testing

At this stage, it was time to bring the product to life. Based on all the insights and data gathered I began designing the new website in collaboration with the team. This stage was also the moment of truth as we ran usability tests and gathered stakeholder & user feedback on the redesign .

Diving deep into Big Picture Philadelphia

Stepping into the project, we first needed to understand the organization, how it works and what role the website plays for the org. Spearheading the research plan, I gathered detailed overview of the BPP's mission & values. Performing a content audit for the website & insights gathered from interviewing 3 stakeholders formed the foundation of our next steps.

PROBLEM DISCOVERY

01

USABILITY TEST - TREE TEST & TASK ANALYSIS

To gain a comprehensive understanding of how users interact with Big Picture Philadelphia's website, we conducted a series of targeted usability tests with 3 users. Our focus was on identifying user pain points, assessing ease of use, and evaluating overall user experience. These findings laid the groundwork for our problem definition and subsequent redesign strategy, ensuring our solutions directly addressed real user needs and challenges.

Tree Test - Key Findings & Takeaways

We began with a tree test to evaluate the website's information architecture. This method helped us understand how easily users could find specific information within the site's structure.

Usability Test & User Interview- Key Findings & Takeaways

Following the tree test, we conducted in-depth task analyses with three participants from our target user group: working professionals. This approach allowed us to observe real-time interactions and gather qualitative data on user behavior. Here are the main takeaways.

Only 30%

of users were able to successfully complete "make a donation"  & "become a mentor" task

Talking to users revealed that besides confusing IA, the information failed to build trust & left them with lot of unanswered questions - eventually turning them away.

Clutter & confusion

and confusion terms were frequently used by users to describe their website experience

The website seemed to have information overload where the user was unable to walk away with any meaningful information.

Stakeholder Interviews - Key Findings & Takeaways

Upon talking with the stakeholders - the Associate Director of Grants & Strategic Communications and Director of School Systems and Supports, I was able to extrapolate the below insights and understand BPP's vision and purpose for the website. 

CHALLENGE

Stakeholder interviews reflected that contrary to our assumptions, the website was not aimed at students or new parents, in fact it aimed to bring in more mentors & attract new donors

SOLUTION

With this new information, we quickly pivoted to the new target user & reassessed our research insights from donor & mentor perspective. It also helped that our user group were working professionals who fit donor & mentor persona

VISZUALIZING THE PAIN POINTS

In this phase, we synthesized our user research to form a comprehensive picture of the overall user experience. We created two user personas representing our target audience: Donors & Mentors along with two user journeys to represent each user's experience. By mapping these journeys, we gained valuable insights into areas needing improvement and opportunities for enhancing the website's functionality for both donors and mentors.

Persona - Generous George / Goal: to donate to a non-profit

User Journey / Goal: to donate to a non-profit

Persona - Activist Andy / Goal: To volunteer & mentor students

User Journey / Goal: to sign up as a mentor

Pinpointing priorities & strategies

Having a deeper understanding of the organization's goals for the website, target audience and the pain points of user's journey through the website, we were able to hone down on the key problem areas and a design statement that guided the content strategy & the new information architecture.

PROBLEM DISCOVERY

02

SALVAGING THE WEBSITE - THE GOOD & THE BAD

While research reflected that the website fails to cater to its target audience - Donors & Mentors, we also felt that there were things that did work. The team & I analyzed the existing site to identify effective and ineffective elements, ensuring efficient use of resources and providing research-backed justification for changes to clients.

THE GOOD

1.

Easy to find Donate button, just needs to be more prominent

2.

Student's success stories highlighting the impact mentors have on their learning

3.

Easy to find mission & values of the organization

AREAS OF IMPROVEMENT

1.

Need secured payments page with options.

2.

Lacks clear instructions on mentor intake, process & requirements

3.

Very text heavy content with some sections failing to pass AAA accessibility standards such as contrast

4.

Important info is hidden under smaller FAQ sections with unclear info

DESIGN GOALS

Preserving brand identity

Visually pleasing

Interactive & easy flowing

Precise & focused

CONTENT STRATEGY 

Our content should help our users/customers understand the mission and values, find testimonials from previous volunteers and get latest updates on events happening from the organization community.

Shaping the blueprint for redesign

We iterated on the new information architecture and content strategy through open card sorting exercises with 8 users followed by a follow up tree test for proposed IA. These revealed users' mental schemas, informing our design decisions. The result is a proposed information architecture that aligns with user expectations and sets the foundation for an intuitive website structure.

SOLUTION DISCOVERY & SCOPING

03

OPEN CARD SORTING - TAKEAWAYS

Given the confusing navigation of the existing website, the team & I performed an open card sort activity with 8 users to further define the pages into relatable buckets. I was able to extrapolate the key themes and patterns that helped define the new navigation for BPP.

Key design decisions based on results

01

Dividing the Get To Know Us section in to two parts

02

Keeping the Get Involved header same and creating a separate header for Contact Us.

03

Removing the For Families header and placing the content under relevant sections.

04

Creating a separate highlighted button for Donate Now.

THE PROPOSED NAV BAR
TREE TESTING THE UPDATED NAVIGATION

I decided to validate the new nav bar and information architecture through a tree test - excitingly, it turned out to be a great success! The new nav bar was 89.8% effective in wayfinding and resonating with users mental schemas.

Bringing it all together

The team & I focused on combining all the information gathered into an effective redesign for the website. Our main focus was to keep the design clean & easy to navigate while also keeping the branding alive with a little bit of playfulness of a student focused organization. Take a look at the final designs below.

EXECUTION & FEEDBACK

04

MID-FI WIREFRAMES
REFRESHED STYLE GUIDE & BRANDING

The team & I collaborated on the style guide and nailing down a refreshed look for the website. The existing website had an overpowered green UI which left the user overwhelmed and confused with content vs. CTA vs. key highlights. Our goal was to simplify the feel while keeping the elements unique and easily recognizable for users.

 

My main focus for this phase was to assure the styling adhered to our design goals and the existing branding of BPP while putting together a cohesive UI guide with the team. 

Final Design & Decisions

There was so much information to be shared that it ended up making the users overwhelmed and leaving the website without any actionable step. To simplify this, I incorporated question headings like "How we spend your donations" based on common questions users had. Pairing this with clear call-to-actions led to significant increase in user engagement & trust.

CLEAR CTA WITH CONVERSATIONAL HEADINGS

During task analysis & usability testing, we observed how users often felt unsure of what was the best way for them to get involved with the org. To reduce this decision fatigue we decided to guide them through bite-sized overview for ways to get involved and easily picking the right fit for them. We also chose to highlight mentoring as that was one of the key needs for the org.

GUIDING USERS WITH BITE-SIZED INFORMATION

Testing revealed users seeking a sitemap in the footer for quick navigation. As a result, we added a comprehensive sitemap to improve usability and also incorporated a newsletter signup to boost user retention.

FUNCTIONAL FOOTER + SITE MAP

The initial website presented a slideshow of student experiences at BPP which gave users a good first insight on the organization. We decided to take it a step further from static pictures and leverage BPP's large library of student experience videos and highlight it as an interactive hero section. 

INTERACTIVE HERO SECTION
Reflecting on project outcomes

This project was a great challenge that allowed me to expand my skills as a designer. Not only did I have to focus on UX & the design but also hit the ground running with project managing skills and keeping the team on the same page. 

05

DESIGNER LEARNINGS

01

Leading with empathy and adaptability

This project taught me the value of empathetic leadership and flexible management. With my team juggling other jobs and stakeholders managing multiple responsibilities, I learned to create a supportive environment, prioritize effectively, and maintain clear communication. I found that adapting to team constraints while maintaining project quality was key to achieving successful outcomes.

02

Efficiency in redesign 

I had to quickly learn the value of strategic resource allocation in redesign. By analyzing the existing website to identify effective elements, I focused our efforts on areas truly needing improvement. This approach allowed us to maintain consistency for current users while efficiently addressing pain points, proving that a targeted redesign can be more impactful and cost-effective than a complete overhaul.
